why: riskiest unknowns first: JDK 25 with AGP 9 and Gradle 9.1, and the emulator on macOS 27

decision: ran four parallel explorers over the iOS app (protocol, TCA state, UI, platform) and kept their findings as files
why: porting agents need a shared, cited map of the iOS app, and keeping it in files keeps the coordinator's context small
result: state.md 607 lines: 8 features, 221 action cases, 25 behaviors a port can get wrong

decision: ran a three-model arena (opus, gpt, grok) to design the Kotlin TCA kit and naming rules, each candidate compiled with worked ports and tests
why: the kit is a one-way door under ~30k Kotlin lines, and line-by-line portability of iOS diffs is the user's long-term requirement

decision: built scripts/ios-sync.py with status, plan, progress, check and advance, keyed on @file:PortedFrom markers in the Kotlin files
why: the mapping lives next to the code it describes so an agent editing a file sees and updates it; check fails on any unclassified, unported, or stale iOS file
result: dry run against 4fb5e0e~3 listed 8 commits and mapped every changed file; check reports 135 port files missing

decision: found upstream main already 5 commits past the explored commit (fdf4b7a, iOS 26 required, variable blur removed); will rebase the port baseline to the latest main before porting starts
why: porting from the newest iOS code avoids replaying today's changes right after the port lands
